description: Under OFAC 31 CFR 560.543, only property owned before becoming a US person, or property inherited, may be sold and proceeds transferred without special permission. All other cases require a specific OFAC licence.
US banks cannot process payments directly involving Iranian banks, so transfers route through non-SDN intermediaries in the UAE, Turkey, Oman or Qatar, with funds converted to euros or dirhams first.
Bypassing banking restrictions via crypto, hawala or unlicensed money transmitters has led to enforcement actions with asset freezes, large fines and imprisonment.
energy_note: The workaround everyone uses is also a felony.

description: Sale proceeds are deposited into a rial account that must then be converted to hard currency, and moving large foreign exchange out needs Central Bank approval. A property transfer tax of about 5% applies.

aspect: Inherited property cannot always be kept
description: A foreign national inheriting Iranian property gets valid ownership, but Iranian law does not permit indefinite foreign ownership - the heir is typically required to transfer it to a qualified person.
energy_note: Forced sale of the family home, on someone else's timetable.

aspect: And then the IRS wants to know
description: Cash inheritance over USD 100,000 from a foreign estate, or non-cash over that value, must be reported to the IRS. Gains on sales of non-commercial Iranian real estate are reportable in the year of sale.
